meta.title: Week 4 Network Analysis: Communities, Overlap, Weights & Backbones

louvain_vs_infomap.interpretation: Louvain optimizes modularity (global density contrast), grouping thinkers into broad historical epochs. Infomap relies on flow dynamics (random walks), capturing localized information diffusion. Disagreements highlight boundary thinkers whose influence flows across multiple distinct movement hubs.

aristotle_overlap.argument: Aristotle cannot be restricted to a single tradition. Through k-clique percolation, he acts as a nexus overlapping Classical Antiquity, Scholastic Theology, and Modern Rationalism. Link-community analysis reveals his outgoing edges belong to fundamentally different functional clusters.

backbone_analysis.interpretation: As alpha decreases, weak statistical correlations drop. At alpha = 0.15, the network fragments as key bridge links from Aristotle dissolve.

weighted_vs_unweighted.summary: Unweighted networks treat structural proximity equally, whereas weighted networks pull thinkers closer based on citation intensity. Nodes shifting between paradigms reveal philosophers who are structurally connected to one school but intellectually tied to another.
